Marissa / Redwood team,

Thanks for the draft MSAs; attached is our redline for the MSA and Order Form. A few points from legal that matter most for us:

- Liability ceiling: we propose a cap equal to the fees paid under the Order Form in the 12 months prior to the claim (i.e., annualized cap).

Marissa — quick thoughts from commercial/finance perspective:

- Prefer aggregate (contract-wide) cap expressed as a multiple of fees paid over the Contract Year or Total Contract Value. Our commercial floor has been 2x annual fees (aggregate), which balances recoverability with predictable exposure.
- Annual reset is workable but increases churn risk for high-growth customers and complicates reconciliation; if we accept annualization, propose a multiplier (e.g., 1.5x of annual fees) rather than plain 1x.
- Carve-outs: IP indemnity and willful misconduct as carve-outs is standard. Strongly push back on broad consequential carve-in for data breach — if we must make an exception, limit it to statutory liability and expressly require causation and a damages threshold.

Negotiation bullets to propose:
1) Liability limited to the greater of (i) $100,000 and (ii) 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months, aggregated across the term (or alternative: 1.5x if annual reset is insisted).
2) Carve-outs for IP indemnity, willful misconduct/gross negligence, and personal injury.
3) Consequential damages remain excluded; carve-in for data privacy only where statutory damages are mandated and proven.

If legal is comfortable, we can offer the annual-reset compromise (1.5x annual fees) as a concession for a faster signature.

-Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Apr 2028 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood MSA - liability ceiling and carve-outs (legal view)

Team — legal view and precedent:

- Precedent: For customers of this profile (mid-market to enterprise SaaS), we typically accept either an aggregate cap of 2x annual fees or an annualized cap at 1.5x annual fees. The aggregate cap is preferable for Redwood to avoid mid-contract exposure divergence.
- Carve-outs: IP indemnity and willful misconduct should remain uncapped. "Personal injury/bodily harm" carve-out is reasonable but rarely triggered in our product; we can keep for commercial optics.
- Data breaches: recommend narrowing the data-breach carve-in to (a) statutory fines/penalties and (b) third-party claims directly caused by Redwood's breach where indemnity applies. Explicitly exclude speculative consequential losses (lost profits) tied to downstream business interruption.

Suggested language to propose back to Acme (short):
"NOTWITHSTANDING THE FOREGOING, THE LIABILITY CAP SHALL NOT APPLY TO (I) LIABILITY ARISING FROM WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR GROSS NEGLIGENCE, (II) INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY INDEMNITY, OR (III) LIABILITY FOR BODILY INJURY OR DEATH. EXCEPT AS SET FORTH IN CLAUSE (B) BELOW, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, AND PUNITIVE DAMAGES ARE DISCLAIMED. CLAUSE (B): STATUTORY DAMAGES AND THIRD-PARTY LIABILITY DIRECTLY CAUSED BY A REDWOOD DATA SECURITY BREACH SHALL BE SUBJECT TO THE LIABILITY CAP BUT LIMITED TO STATUTORY AMOUNTS OR THIRD-PARTY JUDGMENTS; LOST PROFITS AND OTHER INDIRECT LOSSES REMAIN EXCLUDED."

I can produce a redline with the 2x aggregate cap and the narrowed data-breach carve-in language if you want — attached is the internal playbook excerpt I referenced.

-S
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Redwood MSA - liability ceiling and carve-outs (initial redline)

Jordan — thanks for the redline and the clarity on Acme's position. We've reviewed internally and wanted to propose a consolidated position to keep momentum: 

Our proposed position (Redwood):
- Liability cap: aggregate cap equal to 2x the fees paid under the Order Form in the 12 months prior to a claim, aggregated across the Term. This gives both sides predictability while capping our exposure in a commercially meaningful way.
- Alternative compromise: if Acme requires an annual reset, Redwood can accept an annual cap of 1.5x of fees paid in the prior 12 months (per year).
- Carve-outs: uncapped liability remains for (i) willful misconduct or gross negligence, (ii) intellectual property indemnity obligations, and (iii) bodily injury or death.
- Consequential damages: remain excluded. Data security incidents — statutory fines/penalties and third-party judgments directly caused by Redwood are limited to the liability cap (per the language below); lost profits and other indirect losses remain excluded. We are open to objective thresholds and a causation requirement if Acme wants further clarity.

Attached is a redline that implements the above (Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx). If Acme prefers the annual reset path, we can mark an acceptance of 1.5x annual fees to expedite approval.

Next steps: please confirm whether Acme prefers the aggregate 2x approach or the annual reset compromise. If you pick aggregate, we should be able to move to procurement signatures quickly.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.docx (23 KB)]
